title: How to Track Brand Visibility in AI Search (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Learn how to track brand visibility in AI search across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini: prompts, metrics, cadence and tools that actually work.
keywords: how to track brand mentions in AI
how to measure brand visibility in AI search
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
To track brand visibility in AI search, run a fixed set of buyer-style prompts through ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini on a regular schedule. Each time, record whether your brand is mentioned, where it appears, how it is described and which competitors and sources show up. Because AI answers change from run to run, sample each prompt several times and track trends, not single answers. You can do this by hand in a spreadsheet or automate it with a dedicated AI visibility tracker.

## Why tracking AI visibility is different from tracking search rankings

A Google results page is a ranked list of links, and the same query usually returns roughly the same order for most people. An AI assistant writes an answer. It may recommend three brands, ten brands or none at all, and the wording and selection can change between two runs of the same prompt.

That changes what "tracking" means:

- **There is no fixed position to check.** You measure how *often* you appear across many runs, not one rank.
- **The description matters as much as the mention.** An AI answer can name you and still get your pricing, features or category wrong.
- **Sources drive answers.** Assistants that browse the web (Perplexity, ChatGPT with search, Gemini, Google AI Overviews) pull from specific pages. Knowing which pages they cite tells you where to act.
- **Classic tools can't see it.** Rank trackers, Google Analytics and classic alert or social listening feeds don't record what ChatGPT says in a private conversation.

If you're new to the topic, our [AI brand visibility guide](/blog/ai-brand-visibility-guide) explains the concepts. This post is about measurement.

## Which AI platforms to track

Cover the assistants your buyers actually use. For most brands that means four platforms plus Google's AI features:

| Platform | How it answers | What to watch |
|---|---|---|
| **ChatGPT** | Training data, plus [live web search](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt) when it decides to (or when the user asks) | Mention rate, position in lists, accuracy of descriptions, cited links when search runs |
| **Claude** | Training data, plus [web search](https://claude.com/resources/articles/web-search), which Anthropic made available on all Claude plans in 2025 | Whether you're known at all, how your category is framed |
| **Perplexity** | Searches the web for almost every query and shows numbered citations | Which of your pages (and third-party pages) get cited |
| **Google Gemini** | Google's models with access to Google Search | Overlap with your organic rankings, cited sources |
| **Google AI Overviews** | AI summary shown above some Google results | Whether you're named or linked in the overview for your key queries |

A brand can be a standard recommendation in Perplexity and missing from a Claude answer that didn't trigger a search, because one relies on live search for almost every query and the other often answers from training data, so single-platform checks mislead. For platform-specific tactics, see our guides on [tracking ChatGPT brand mentions](/blog/how-to-track-chatgpt-brand-mentions) and [Perplexity SEO](/perplexity-seo).

For Google AI Overviews, search your priority queries in a private window and note whether an overview appears and names or links you. Google's guide to [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) explains how these features draw on Search. Some SEO platforms now report AI answers alongside rankings; for example, Ahrefs Brand Radar lists AI Overviews and AI Mode among its tracked platforms (as of October 2026).

## How to track brand visibility in AI manually, step by step

The manual method costs nothing but time and teaches you how AI assistants see your market. It's the right place to start, even if you automate later.

### Step 1: Define your brand, competitors and category terms

Write down:

- Your brand name plus common variants and misspellings (e.g. "Acme CRM", "AcmeCRM", "Acme")
- 3–8 direct competitors you want to benchmark against
- The words buyers use for your category ("CRM for small business", "sales pipeline software")

### Step 2: Build a prompt set by intent

Don't just ask "What is [brand]?" That only tells you whether the model knows you exist. Real buyers ask category and problem questions where you have to *earn* the mention. Group prompts into four intents:

**Category prompts** (discovery: are you on the shortlist?)

```
What are the best CRM tools for small businesses?
Recommend project management software for a 20-person agency.
Top alternatives to spreadsheets for tracking sales leads?
```

**Comparison prompts** (consideration: how do you stack up?)

```
Acme CRM vs HubSpot: which is better for a small sales team?
Compare Pipedrive, Acme CRM and Zoho for ease of use.
What are the best alternatives to Salesforce?
```

**Problem prompts** (unbranded pain points your product solves)

```
How can I stop losing track of follow-ups with sales leads?
What's the easiest way to see my whole sales pipeline in one place?
```

**Brand prompts** (accuracy: what does the AI believe about you?)

```
What is Acme CRM and who is it for?
How much does Acme CRM cost?
What are the pros and cons of Acme CRM?
```

Start with 20–40 prompts weighted toward category and problem intent, since that's where new customers discover brands. Write them the way a real person would type them, including context like company size, budget or location when it matters to your market. Keep the wording frozen once you start; changing a prompt resets its history.

### Step 3: Control your testing conditions

AI answers are influenced by memory, chat history, account personalization and location. To keep results comparable:

- Use a fresh chat for every prompt (no previous conversation in the thread)
- Turn off memory or custom instructions where possible, or use a clean account
- Note the model or mode used (for example, whether web search was on)
- Note your location, or test from the region that matters to your customers

Write down what you can't control; it explains odd results later.

### Step 4: Sample each prompt multiple times

This is the step most manual audits skip. Run the same prompt once and you get one possible answer, not *the* answer. Run each prompt **at least 3 times per platform** per tracking cycle (5 is better for your most important prompts) and count how many runs mention you.

"Mentioned in 3 of 5 runs" is a far more honest data point than "mentioned" or "not mentioned." It also stops you from overreacting when a single answer drops your brand.

### Step 5: Record the same fields every time

Use one row per prompt run. A simple spreadsheet works:

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-10-20 |
| Platform / model | Perplexity (default) |
| Prompt ID + intent | P07 – category |
| Run # | 2 of 5 |
| Brand mentioned? | Yes |
| Position | 3rd of 6 brands |
| Competitors mentioned | HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho |
| Sentiment / framing | Neutral, "affordable option" |
| Accuracy issues | Lists a discontinued plan |
| Sources cited | G2 review page, a 2025 listicle, our pricing page |
| Notes | Web search on; US location |

Save the full answer text or a screenshot too, so you can work out *why* something changed.

## The metrics that matter

At the end of each cycle, calculate these six metrics per platform and overall, then compare them with the previous cycle.

### Mention rate

The share of prompt runs in which your brand appears. If you ran 30 prompts 3 times each (90 runs) and were mentioned in 27, your mention rate is 30%. Track it overall and per intent. A low rate on category prompts with a high rate on brand prompts means the AI knows you but doesn't recommend you.

### Position

When you're mentioned in a list, where do you appear? Being first carries more weight than being sixth in a list of six. Record the position and the list length, then average across runs where you were mentioned.

### Share of voice

Your mentions divided by the total mentions of you and your tracked competitors across the same prompts. If you were mentioned 27 times and your four competitors totaled 108, your share of voice is 27 / 135 = 20%. This is the best single number for competitive benchmarking.

### Sentiment and framing

Is the mention positive, neutral or negative, and what label does the AI attach to you ("best for enterprises", "budget pick", "hard to set up")? Framing often matters more than raw sentiment because it decides which buyers the AI sends your way.

### Citations and sources

For platforms that cite sources, record which URLs appear when you are mentioned, and which appear when competitors are mentioned and you aren't. This is the most actionable data you'll collect: it tells you which review sites, comparison articles, directories and pages of your own the AI trusts.

### Accuracy

Flag factual errors: wrong pricing, missing features, outdated product names, wrong category, confusion with a similarly named company. Accuracy problems are often the fastest wins, because you can fix the source content they come from.

For a deeper look at scoring, see our guide on [how to choose an AI brand visibility tracker](/blog/ai-brand-visibility-tracker).

## How often to track

There's no universal right cadence, but these work well in practice:

- **Monthly:** a full run of your prompt set across all platforms. Good enough for most brands to see trends.
- **Weekly or every two weeks:** your 5–10 most important category prompts, if you're actively working on visibility or in a competitive category.
- **After major events:** a product launch, rebrand, pricing change, big PR moment, or a known AI model update. Models and their search behavior change over time, and those shifts can move your visibility without you doing anything. Our post on [AI model drift detection](/blog/ai-model-drift-detection) covers how to spot this.

Whatever cadence you choose, keep it consistent. Trends only mean something if each cycle uses the same prompts and conditions.

### The honest limits of AI visibility tracking

Be clear with your team about what the numbers can't tell you:

- **Answers vary per run.** Small samples swing by chance; look for consistent movement across cycles.
- **Personalization exists.** Real users with memory and history may see different answers.
- **Location and language matter.** US results may differ from UK or German ones.
- **Models change.** A new model version can reshuffle recommendations overnight.
- **No platform publishes prompt volumes.** Choose prompts from buyer research, not search volume.

## Tools for tracking brand mentions in AI: what actually covers AI answers

A common mistake is assuming a classic brand monitoring setup covers this. Usually it doesn't. [Google Alerts](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/4815696) emails you when new results for a topic show up in Google Search, and classic social listening feeds watch the public web, news and social media. AI conversations aren't published pages, so those feeds can't see what ChatGPT or Claude says when someone asks for a recommendation. That said, some listening vendors now sell separate AI modules: Brand24 offers [AI Visibility](https://brand24.com/ai-visibility/) (powered by Chatbeat) and Meltwater offers [GenAI Lens](https://www.meltwater.com/en/products/genai-lens), both of which run prompts through AI assistants. Check exactly which assistants and prompts any tool covers before you rely on it.

| Approach | Covers AI answers? | Strengths | Limitations | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Manual prompting + spreadsheet** | Yes | Free, flexible, you see every answer firsthand | Slow; hard to sample enough runs; easy to drift from consistent conditions | First audits, small prompt sets, learning your landscape |
| **Dedicated AI visibility tools** (e.g. AI Brand Track and others) | Yes | Query several AIs at once, calculate mention rate / share of voice / sentiment automatically, repeatable | Costs money; each tool covers different platforms and prompt types | Ongoing tracking, competitor benchmarking, reporting |
| **Classic brand monitoring** (Google Alerts, social listening feeds) | No (some vendors sell separate AI add-ons) | Catches web, news, review and social mentions | The core web and social feeds don't see AI-generated answers | PR, reputation, finding the sources AI may learn from |
| **SEO platforms** (rank trackers, Search Console) | Partly (some suites now have AI visibility add-ons) | Shows organic rankings that feed AI search | Search Console doesn't report ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity answers; add-on coverage varies by vendor | Understanding the search layer underneath AI answers |

Traditional monitoring still has a role: the reviews, articles and forum threads it finds are often the same sources AI assistants cite. It just isn't AI visibility tracking.

## How to act on your results

Tracking only pays off if it changes what you do. Use your data to choose actions by diagnosis:

1. **Mentioned for brand prompts, missing from category prompts.** The AI knows you but doesn't associate you with the category. Publish clear pages that state what you are, who you serve and how you compare (category pages, comparison pages, "alternatives to X" pages), and work on being included in third-party roundups and review sites.
2. **Competitors cited from sources you're absent from.** Look at the cited URLs. If the same review site, directory or listicle keeps appearing, getting listed or reviewed there is often the most direct path into the answer.
3. **Inaccurate descriptions.** Find where the wrong information comes from (old press releases, outdated directory listings, your own stale pages) and correct it. Make pricing, features and positioning easy to find and consistent everywhere.
4. **Visible on Perplexity and Gemini, missing in Claude or ChatGPT without search.** Search-based assistants reflect your current web presence; training-based answers lag behind. Keep building authoritative mentions and expect a slower response.
5. **Negative or off-target framing.** Address the underlying cause (reviews, documentation, positioning) and publish content that clearly answers the objection.
6. **Weak position in comparisons.** Create honest, specific comparison content and make your differentiators concrete enough for an AI to repeat.

Then re-run the same prompts in your next cycle and check whether the metrics moved. For the optimization side in depth, read [how to get your brand mentioned in ChatGPT](/blog/how-to-get-your-brand-mentioned-in-chatgpt) and our overview of [generative engine optimization](/generative-engine-optimization).

## A simple tracking plan to start this week

- **Day 1:** List your brand variants, 5 competitors and 25 prompts across the four intents.
- **Day 2–3:** Run each prompt 3 times on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini in fresh chats. Log every run.
- **Day 4:** Calculate mention rate, average position, share of voice and accuracy issues. List the top 10 cited sources.
- **Day 5:** Pick three actions from the diagnosis list above.
- **Next month:** Re-run the same set and compare. Automate once the manual workload becomes the bottleneck. With 25 prompts × 3 runs × 4 platforms, that's 300 answers per cycle, which is when many teams [start with a free automated analysis](/register).

## FAQ

### How do I track brand mentions in ChatGPT?

Open a fresh chat with memory turned off and ask a fixed set of category, comparison, problem and brand prompts. Run each prompt several times, recording whether you're mentioned, your position, the competitors named and any cited links when ChatGPT uses web search. Repeat on a regular schedule, or use an AI visibility tool to automate the queries.

### Is it possible to track brand mentions in AI search?

Yes, but not with traditional monitoring tools, because AI answers are generated per conversation and not published on the web. You track them by querying the assistants directly with consistent prompts and measuring results across many runs. Because answers vary, the result is a rate (for example, mentioned in 40% of runs) rather than a fixed ranking.

### How do you measure brand visibility in AI search?

Measure mention rate (how often you appear), position (where you appear in lists), share of voice (your mentions vs competitors'), sentiment and framing, the sources cited, and accuracy of what the AI says about you. Calculate these per platform and per prompt intent, then compare over time. Many tools combine them into a single visibility score.

### How do I track brand mentions in general?

For the open web, news and social media, use brand monitoring tools such as Google Alerts or a social listening platform. For AI assistants, you need tracking that actually queries the assistants: manual prompting, a dedicated AI visibility tool, or an AI add-on from a listening or SEO vendor, since web and social feeds can't see AI answers. Most brands now need both.

### What are the key metrics used to track brand awareness?

Traditional brand awareness metrics include branded search volume, share of voice in media and social, direct traffic, mention volume and survey-based aided and unaided recall. In AI search, the equivalents are AI mention rate, share of voice in AI answers, position in recommendations and sentiment. Together they show whether people and AI systems both know and recommend your brand.

### How do I get my brand mentioned by AI?

Be clearly described, consistently, on the sources AI assistants rely on: your own site, review platforms, industry directories, comparison articles and credible publications. Publish pages that answer the exact questions buyers ask, keep facts like pricing up to date, and earn third-party coverage. Then track whether your mention rate improves.
